name: Clean and validate derived walls
instructions: Run this step after deriving the first wall layer and before placing doors.
A valid wall tile must be part of a meaningful room, hallway, or exterior boundary.
Remove isolated wall stubs, comb teeth, one-tile wall fragments, and wall pockets that do not enclose or separate useful floor regions.
Do not use wall tiles as decorative filler or padding.
Do not create small wall columns along hallway edges unless they are part of a continuous boundary between a room and the hallway.
A wall tile should usually have floor on at least one cardinal side and either outside/empty or another floor region on the opposite side.
If a derived wall creates a jagged tooth pattern along a hallway, simplify the floorplan or move the boundary before door placement.
If cleanup would expose a floor to outside, revise the floor region shape instead of adding a second wall layer.
After cleanup, every floor region must still be enclosed by exactly one wall layer before doors/windows are cut.
rejectPatterns: isolated wall tile not connected to a useful boundary
wall-door-wall or wall-wall caps backed by another wall layer
dead wall pockets that do not border floor
preferredFixes: move the hallway or room edge before wall derivation
resize an edge or corner room within its allowed size band
